3365	## Creator Partner Program — agency/KOL commission + a real customer discount
3366	
3367	**What it does.** An agency or content creator gets a permanent link. Every customer who signs up
3368	through it is attached to that partner FOR LIFE (one partner per customer, enforced by a DB unique
3369	constraint) and gets a real, sitewide discount for as long as they stay a customer — **50% off their
3370	first purchase of any service except a domain, then 10% off every purchase after that, forever**
3371	(new orders AND renewals). The partner earns a **lifetime commission** (their own negotiated
3372	`commissionRatePct`, default 20%) on every qualifying charge that customer ever makes, with one
3373	carve-out: a dedicated-IP add-on line earns the partner 0% (everything else on the same
3374	order/renewal still earns the full rate).
3375	
3376	This is a DIFFERENT program from "Refer & earn" (`User.referralCode`, the row above this one) — a
3377	peer-to-peer, one-time wallet bonus. A single `?ref=`/`nxeon_ref` cookie can only ever mean ONE of
3378	the two: at registration (`lib/actions.ts` `register()`), an ACTIVE `ReferralPartner.code` match
3379	always wins over a `User.referralCode` match, so nobody double-dips a partner commission AND a peer
3380	referral bonus off the same signup.
3381	
3382	**Data model** (`prisma/schema.prisma`):
3383	
3384	| Model | Purpose |
3385	|---|---|
3386	| `ReferralPartner` | The partner: `code` (unique, uppercase), `commissionRatePct` (per-partner, frozen onto each commission row at accrual), `status` (ACTIVE/PAUSED — pausing stops BOTH new commission AND the customer discount), optional `userId` login |
3387	| `PartnerCustomer` | The lifetime attachment. `customerId` UNIQUE — one partner per customer, ever. `firstPurchaseDiscountUsedAt` (null until their first discounted purchase; null = 50% tier, set = 10% tier forever) |
3388	| `PartnerCommission` | One row per qualifying PAID invoice, `invoiceId` UNIQUE (idempotent). `baseCents` = net charge minus that invoice's `dedicatedIpCents` — the dedicated-IP exclusion |
3389	| `PartnerPayout` | A REAL payment made to the partner off-wallet (bank/Wise/PayPal), can be partial. Balance = `sum(PartnerCommission, status != VOID) − sum(PartnerPayout)` — NOT derived from commission-row status alone (see the model's own doc comment for why a partial payout needs a separate ledger) |
3390	| `PartnerInvite` | Two kinds (`kind`). `LOGIN`: a pending invite for a brand-new (non-customer) login on an admin-made partner — token-hash/expiry, mirrors `OrgInvite`'s mechanics. `CREATOR` (2026-09-27): an invite made BEFORE any partner exists — `partnerId` is null until claimed; carries `name`, `note`, `ratePct`, `allowAnyEmail`, the CSV prefill (`channelUrl`, `primaryGame`, `country`, `subscribers`), `lastSentAt` (NULL = DRAFT, never emailed) and `sendCount` |
3391	| `PartnerPayoutProfile` (2026-09-27) | One per partner: the partner's own contact fields (plain) + preferred payout method; the method-specific details and note are sealed in `payoutDetailsEnc` with `lib/crypto-box.ts` (AES-256-GCM from `AUTH_SECRET`). `payoutUpdatedAt` shown to admins |
3392	| `ReferralClick` (existing, previously unused) | One row per real link click — `code`, `ipHash`, `referer`, `convertedUserId` (best-effort, set at registration to the most recent unconverted click for that code) |
3393	| `Invoice.dedicatedIpCents` | How much of that invoice's net amount is the dedicated-IP surcharge — a real typed column, populated by every charge path that can bill one (`lib/order.ts`, `lib/game-order.ts`, `worker/billing.ts`), never inferred by parsing line items after the fact |
3394	
3395	**The links.** `nxeon.cloud/partner/<code>` (`app/partner/[code]/route.ts`) is the REAL link partners
3396	are given — it records a `ReferralClick` row, then sets the `nxeon_ref` cookie and 302s to
3397	`/register`, exactly like the older `/r/<code>` (peer-referral short link), which now ALSO records a
3398	click (same table — its own schema comment always said it covers both code namespaces).
3399	
3400	**Automatic attachment.** `register()` (`lib/actions.ts`) reads `nxeon_ref`; if it matches an ACTIVE
3401	partner code, `attachCustomerToPartnerByCode` (`lib/partner-commission.ts`) creates the
3402	`PartnerCustomer` row right there — no admin action needed for the normal case. `adminAttachCustomer`
3403	(`lib/actions-partner.ts`) remains for support/edge cases (attaching an existing account by email).
3404	
3405	**The customer discount** — pure math in `lib/partner-discount.ts` (`PARTNER_FIRST_PURCHASE_PCT` =
3406	50, `PARTNER_RECURRING_PCT` = 10), DB resolution in `lib/partner-pricing.ts`
3407	(`partnerDiscountForNewOrder`, `partnerDiscountForRenewal`, `partnerPreviewForCode`/`ForUser` for
3408	pre-purchase marketing messaging). Wired into:
3409	- `lib/order.ts` `orderQuote`/`placeOrder` (VPS) and `lib/game-order.ts` `gameOrderQuote`/
3410	  `placeGameOrder` (game servers) — the discount is folded into `chargeCents` itself (displayed ===
3411	  charged), gets its OWN line on the invoice, and the first-purchase slot is claimed ATOMICALLY
3412	  inside the same transaction that debits the wallet (`claimPartnerFirstPurchase`) — a lost race (the
3413	  same customer's own concurrent "first" order) keeps the already-quoted price rather than
3414	  recomputing mid-transaction (an accepted, narrow, low-severity edge case: a customer can only ever
3415	  race against their OWN other order).
3416	- `lib/renewal-charge.ts` `renewalCharge` — `RenewalPrices.partnerDiscountPercent` (optional, 0 by
3417	  default), always resolved via `partnerDiscountForRenewal` (a renewal is never anyone's first
3418	  purchase), stacks with the pre-existing one-time retention offer (retention first, partner discount
3419	  on what's left). Wired into every real renewal path in `worker/billing.ts` (the automatic sweep,
3420	  the saved-card auto-charge, the renewal-reminder email amount, the suspended-account
3421	  auto-recovery) and `lib/actions.ts` `renewNow`.
3422	- **Visible before the first purchase**, per the product requirement: the public `/pricing` page
3423	  reads the `nxeon_ref` cookie (anonymous) or the real attachment (signed in) and shows a real banner;
3424	  the deploy wizard (`components/nx/DeployView.tsx`) shows a live "Partner discount — 50%/10% off"
3425	  badge next to the coupon/promo badges, sourced from the same `orderQuote`/`gameOrderQuote` result
3426	  the wizard already prices from (`lib/nx/quote.ts`, `lib/nx/quote-game.ts`) — not a second formula.
3427	- **Hosting, business email and domains do NOT carry this discount yet** (domains are excluded by

# Part VII — Change history

Everything below this line is **history**, not reference. It is kept because the *reasons* recorded in
these entries are often the only surviving explanation for why a piece of code looks the way it does.
Where an entry contradicts Parts I–VI, **Parts I–VI win** — they were verified against the tree; these
were written at the time.

## How to read the change history

```
 Part VII is ordered oldest → newest in three layers:
   1. "Change history — the first 28 commits"   the compressed early record
   2. dated / titled entries                    one H2 per shipped change
   3. "Session log — 2026-07-26/27"             the most recent waves
 Authoritative alternatives when an entry looks stale:
   git log --date=short --pretty='%h|%ad|%s'
   git blame <file> -L <start>,<end>
```

## Session log — 2026-07-26 into 2026-07-27 (the customer-readiness push)

Seven commits, newest first. This document was last verified at `4ea9790`; everything above it in this
table is what the current pass folded in.

| Commit | Subject | Verified state |
|---|---|---|
| `2d8fedd` | Game servers renew at their game-plan price, not the base VPS plan | **Real.** `renewalQuote` delegates to `renewalCharge` and owns no arithmetic; a test asserts the file contains none. The extraction of `lib/renewal-charge.ts` was forced by a bundling failure (`Can't resolve 'fs'`) that `tsc` could not see |
| `f28f15e` | Refuse truncated Stripe metadata; one quote per order; honest receipt | **Real.** `packMetadata` throws before `checkout.sessions.create`; the sold price rides in metadata; the receipt attaches an invoice or points at billing history, never promises one it does not send |
| `3aa24d7` | Verification gates, auth lockouts, email verification (gate ships OFF) | **Mixed by design.** The two auth lockouts and the NAT flush are genuinely fixed. Email verification is **complete and deliberately disarmed** — `email_verification_enforced` defaults to `false` because the platform's DKIM record is missing (gaps 1 and 9). Two of the three agents behind this commit were killed mid-task; what is recorded here is what was verified afterwards, not what was intended |
| `7490131` | Stop charging customers without consent; card-save UI | **Real.** Three launch blockers from `docs/QA-JOURNEY.md`, all reproduced in a browser and all byte-identical in production, plus the card-save UI that had been wrongly marked complete |
| `156b6ac` | Harden the post-cutover TLS sweep against its own first live run | **Real, and verified on the live queue** rather than asserted: jobs drain, the permanent path settles, notifications stopped climbing |
| `4ea9790` | Promo-basis proration, post-cutover TLS, 8 more migration defects | **Real.** `Server.termPromoPercent` makes the proration round trip net zero by construction; the TLS pass stopped being dead code; 4 rows backfilled from real billing records with 0 fallbacks |
| `fd71056` | Migration rehearsal fixes, proration symmetry, wallet floor, CI | **Real.** Nine engine defects, the `capMonths` asymmetry, the sub-Stripe-floor card leg, and the first CI workflow |

The through-line across all seven is the defect this codebase keeps producing in new places: **a second
definition of something that already had one.** A second renewal formula. A second promo basis. A
second place `lastAutoBackup` could be written. A second email-normalisation. The fix, every time, was
to delete the duplicate rather than to make the two agree.

## Creator Partner Program — tabbed partner dashboard, dated analytics, payout preferences, creator invites (2026-09-27)

- **Tabs**: `/dashboard/partner` is now Overview / Analytics / Customers / Payouts / Media kit /

## feat/partner-code-entry
#!/bin/bash
# Deploy a ref (default: main from /opt/nxeon) to the staging environment.
# Usage: ./scripts/deploy-staging.sh [git-ref]
set -euo pipefail
REF="${1:-main}"
cd /opt/nxeon-staging

echo "==> Syncing staging to $REF"
git fetch origin
git reset --hard "origin/$REF"

echo "==> Installing dependencies"
npm install --no-audit --no-fund 2>&1 | tail -1

echo "==> Applying database schema"
npx prisma db push --accept-data-loss 2>&1 | tail -2
npm run db:seed 2>&1 | tail -2 || true

echo "==> Building"
npm run build 2>&1 | tail -4

# next.config sets output:"standalone" but the systemd unit runs the standalone
# server.js directly (not `next start`, which Next.js explicitly does not
# support alongside output:"standalone" — it prints a warning and silently
# fails to resolve some routes, confirmed live 2026-09-10: a brand-new API
# route 404'd under `next start` on this exact build and returned 200 under
# `node .next/standalone/server.js`). The standalone output does NOT include
# public/ or .next/static/ (Next's own documented behavior) — copy them in
# fresh every build, or every static asset/route added after the last copy
# is missing until the next deploy happens to also touch this step.
echo "==> Copying static assets into the standalone server output"
rm -rf .next/standalone/public .next/standalone/.next/static
cp -r public .next/standalone/public
cp -r .next/static .next/standalone/.next/static
# geoip-lite is in next.config.ts's serverExternalPackages (kept OUT of the JS
# bundle on purpose, since it reads .dat files off its own package path at
# runtime) — but the standalone output tracer only copies files it can trace
# as JS-imported, so an externalized package's own non-JS data files are
# silently left behind. Found live 2026-09-10: this crashed EVERY request
# with an uncaught ENOENT the moment the systemd unit ran the standalone
# server.js instead of `next start` — geo-ip.ts's own try/catch around
# geoip.lookup() does NOT help, because the failure isn't confined to that
# call. Copy the package's real data/ directory in every build, same
# reasoning as public/.next/static above.
if [ -d node_modules/geoip-lite/data ]; then
  mkdir -p .next/standalone/node_modules/geoip-lite/data
  cp -r node_modules/geoip-lite/data/. .next/standalone/node_modules/geoip-lite/data/
fi

# Web runs as the unprivileged 'nxeon' user. Only .next needs to be writable by
# it (Next cache); the rest stays root-owned and world-readable, and systemd
# injects .env as root. Do NOT chown the whole tree (breaks root git on .git).
echo "==> Fixing .next ownership for non-root web"
chown -R nxeon:nxeon /opt/nxeon-staging/.next 2>/dev/null || true
chmod 600 /opt/nxeon-staging/.env 2>/dev/null || true

echo "==> Restarting staging services"
systemctl restart nxeon-staging-web nxeon-staging-worker
sleep 5
systemctl is-active nxeon-staging-web nxeon-staging-worker
CODE=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://127.0.0.1:8080/)
echo "==> Staging responds: HTTP $CODE (http://$(grep ^PUBLIC_IP .env | cut -d= -f2):8080)"
[ "$CODE" = "200" ] || { echo "STAGING UNHEALTHY"; exit 1; }
echo "==> Staging deploy complete"

input.message:
## Summary
All the work is done and running on staging, and I stopped short of production. It is two commits on `feat/partner-code-entry` in `/root/nxeon-worktrees/partner-code`: `68e44c98c3` (creator codes, email masking, payout policy) and `42029d4b0e` (your "minimum payout threshold" wording). The branch is pushed to origin and deployed to staging with `deploy-staging.sh`. Staging was on `promo-trial-798` before this, so it now runs my branch. `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` passes with no errors at all, including Prisma types. The 10 new tests in `test/creator-code.test.ts` and the existing partner-discount suite pass. There was no schema change, and I never ran prisma generate, db push or npm install in the worktree.

## What changed
- **Register page**: there is a new optional "Creator code" field.
  - If the visitor arrived through `/partner/<code>` or `?ref=`, it is pre-filled server-side and looks locked: the code, the creator's name and a "Change" link.
  - `register()` in `lib/actions.ts` checks the typed value server-side, after the existing signup rate limit.
  - A bad code shows an error under the field, and nothing the user typed is lost. Clearing the field lets them sign up without a code.
  - A valid code attaches the creator through the same `attachCustomerToPartnerByCode` the link uses. A typed code that doesn't match the cookie doesn't mark a link click as converted.
  - Clearing a pre-filled code means "no creator". A friend-referral cookie still works as before, and a creator code wins over it (the existing no-double-dip rule).
- **Deploy wizard**: the existing promo box now reads "Promo or creator code". There is no second box.
  - While the user types, `checkCreatorCode` (in the new `lib/actions-creator-code.ts`) looks the code up. It is read-only, needs a signed-in user, and is limited to 40 checks per 10 minutes per account.
  - If the code is a creator code, the coupon message is replaced. An eligible account sees the creator's name, a note that the link is permanent, and an **"Apply creator code"** button. Nothing is attached on a keystroke, because typing SAMSUNG10 passes through SAM.
  - `applyCreatorCode` re-checks every rule inside one database transaction and then attaches the account. It is refused while an admin is impersonating, limited to 10 attempts per 15 minutes per account and IP, and written to the audit log.
  - After that the code leaves the box and the quote re-runs. The existing partner-discount logic picks up the new link, so the quote and the charge come from the same function. A creator code is never submitted as a coupon.
  - All the rules live in the new `lib/creator-code.ts`.
- **Masking**: customer emails are masked server-side before they reach the creator's browser (`lib/mask-email.ts`, e.g. `j•••@g•••.com`). This covers the Customers tab, and the ledger and Analytics events wherever a customer has no name. Admin views are unchanged.
- **Payout policy** (your follow-up requests):
  - The $25 threshold lives in one constant, `MIN_PAYOUT_THRESHOLD_CENTS = 2500` in `lib/partner-payout.ts`. `partnerPayoutPolicyText()` builds the owner's exact sentence from it.
  - That sentence now appears on the Overview, Payouts and Terms tabs and in the invite email's "Payouts" row. The old "paid out on request" and "no schedule or minimum configured" wording is gone.
  - The Terms tab and invite email now say "through your link or by entering your code".
  - It is stated, not enforced; payouts stay manual.
- **Docs**: `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` has a new "Typed creator codes" section and updated Customers, Terms and PDF entries, plus a dated change-history entry. `ROADMAP.md` is updated too.

## Rules I applied
- **Self-referral**: blocked. `attachCustomerToPartnerByCode` already refused to attach a creator's own account, and nothing in the codebase allows it. The message is "That's your own creator code — it can't be used on your own account."
- **Who can attach at checkout** (all four must hold):
  - The account isn't linked to any creator yet. Otherwise: "This account is already linked to a creator." If it's the same creator, it shows "Already linked to …" instead.
  - The account has made no paid purchase. That means no paid or refunded invoice above zero that isn't a wallet top-up (the same test commission accrual uses), and no non-free server. Otherwise: "Creator codes apply to a first purchase — this account has already bought something."
  - The creator is ACTIVE. Otherwise: "This creator code isn't active right now."
  - It isn't the account's own code (above).
- Codes are case-insensitive: trimmed and compared in uppercase.
- **Stacking**: the box holds one code at a time. If a coupon and a creator share the same code, the coupon wins, so every coupon that works today still works. Once a creator code is applied the box is free for a coupon, and they combine exactly as today for link-referred customers: the partner discount comes off after the intro price and coupon. The coupon's own rules are untouched.

## Verified on staging (Playwright, throwaway `@example.com` accounts)
Screenshots 01–14 are in `/tmp/claude-0/-root/ec6fa978-d80b-4147-9982-eea470598e2c/scratchpad/partner-code/`. I never pressed Pay.

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Arrive via `/partner/ADVIDEO` | Field pre-filled and locked; signup linked the account |
| Wizard quote for that account | S$17.41 became S$8.70 with the 50% line; renewal S$15.66 |
| Re-type the same code | "Already linked to Ad Video Partner." |
| Invalid code at signup | Inline error, name and email kept; cleared the field and signed up |
| Wizard, no creator | S$17.41 |
| Invalid code in promo box | "That code isn't valid." |
| Lowercase `advideo` | Eligible panel; hidden coupon field empty |
| Apply | Quote S$8.70 with the partner discount line; linked in the DB; audit row written |
| Linked account tries a second creator's code | "This account is already linked to a creator." |
| Creator uses their own code | Own-code refusal |
| Code typed at signup with no link | Linked; no click credited; 50% in the quote |
| Creator's Customers tab | Email shows as `p•••@e•••.com`; the raw address is nowhere in the page HTML |
| Terms and Payouts tabs | Show the threshold sentence |

- The self-referral and "second creator" cases needed a second creator on staging. Only ADVIDEO existed and the staging admin login is broken, so I inserted a temporary partner (`PCTSELF`) directly into the staging database and deleted it afterwards.
- For the "already bought something" rule, I ran the real code read-only against an existing staging customer who has a paid invoice. It returned that refusal.

## Not verified
- The invite email as rendered. Only the wording is covered by a unit test, since staging has no email sending and no working admin login.
- Game server, hosting and email checkouts with a creator code; I only walked the VPS checkout.
- Mobile widths.
- Payment itself, by design.

## Action for you at promote time
Install the terms PDF:
`install -o nxeon -m 0644 /root/nxeon-creator-invites/terms/Nxeon-Creator-Partner-Terms.pdf /opt/nxeon/partner-files/creator-partner-terms.pdf`
The regenerated PDF has the threshold wording. I did not touch `/opt/nxeon`, and the owner's original PDFs stay unpublished. Two claims in it go further than the code does:
- It says "40% for life", but each partner's rate is set individually (default 20%). That's only true if every creator is set to 40%.
- It says the 50% applies to "any service except domains", but hosting and business email don't get the discount yet. The existing pricing page and partner dashboard already make that same claim.

## Other issues found (not fixed)
- **Worth a separate task**: the game-server checkout never sends the coupon code with the order. The hidden field only exists on the VPS form in `DeployView.tsx`, so a game coupon shown in the quote isn't applied when the customer pays.
- Google and Discord sign-ups never attach a creator from the link cookie. Those customers can now use the checkout box before their first purchase instead.
- Customer names are still shown to creators in full; only emails are masked.
- There is a narrow race: a customer paying at the same moment they apply a code could get linked right after that first purchase.

  - The account has made no paid purchase. That means no paid or refunded invoice above zero that isn't a wallet top-up (the same test commission accrual uses), and no non-free server. Otherwise: "Creator codes apply to a first purchase — this account has already bought something."
  - The creator is ACTIVE. Otherwise: "This creator code isn't active right now."
  - It isn't the account's own code (above).
- Codes are case-insensitive: trimmed and compared in uppercase.
- **Stacking**: the box holds one code at a time. If a coupon and a creator share the same code, the coupon wins, so every coupon that works today still works. Once a creator code is applied the box is free for a coupon, and they combine exactly as today for link-referred customers: the partner discount comes off after the intro price and coupon. The coupon's own rules are untouched.

`install -o nxeon -m 0644 /root/nxeon-creator-invites/terms/Nxeon-Creator-Partner-Terms.pdf /opt/nxeon/partner-files/creator-partner-terms.pdf`
The regenerated PDF has the threshold wording. I did not touch `/opt/nxeon`, and the owner's original PDFs stay unpublished. Two claims in it go further than the code does:
- It says "40% for life", but each partner's rate is set individually (default 20%). That's only true if every creator is set to 40%.
- It says the 50% applies to "any service except domains", but hosting and business email don't get the discount yet. The existing pricing page and partner dashboard already make that same claim.

## Other issues found (not fixed)
- **Worth a separate task**: the game-server checkout never sends the coupon code with the order. The hidden field only exists on the VPS form in `DeployView.tsx`, so a game coupon shown in the quote isn't applied when the customer pays.
- Google and Discord sign-ups never attach a creator from the link cookie. Those customers can now use the checkout box before their first purchase instead.
- Customer names are still shown to creators in full; only emails are masked.
